blocks.text: Four times a year, Turkish streets fill with red-and-white flags for a national holiday. Each one recalls a step in the years between the end of the First World War and the founding of the Republic, and Turks often call them by their dates alone.

**23 Nisan**, *Ulusal Egemenlik ve Çocuk Bayramı* (National Sovereignty and Children's Day), marks the opening of the Grand National Assembly in Ankara on 23 April 1920, during the War of Independence. The day became a national holiday in 1921, and from 1927 it was also celebrated as children's day; a law of 1981 joined the two under the present name. On this day primary-school pupils take the seats of mayors, governors and ministers for a few symbolic hours, schools put on dances and poetry, and the public broadcaster, TRT, invites children's groups from other countries to an international festival.

**19 Mayıs**, *Atatürk'ü Anma, Gençlik ve Spor Bayramı* (Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day), recalls 19 May 1919, when Mustafa Kemal, later Atatürk, landed at Samsun on the Black Sea coast. Turkish history takes that landing as the start of the War of Independence. Since a law of 1938 the day has belonged to young people and sport, with parades, sports events and folk dances.

**30 Ağustos**, *Zafer Bayramı* (Victory Day), marks the battle of 30 August 1922 near Dumlupınar, in western Anatolia, which decided the war; on 9 September Turkish troops entered İzmir. It has been an official holiday since 1926 and is also the day of the Turkish Armed Forces, with ceremonies and parades.

**29 Ekim**, *Cumhuriyet Bayramı* (Republic Day), is the biggest of the four. On 29 October 1923 the Assembly proclaimed the Republic of Turkey, with Mustafa Kemal as its first president. The holiday starts at one in the afternoon on 28 October. Towns hold parades in the morning and concerts and fireworks in the evening; in Istanbul the fireworks light up the Bosphorus.

blocks.title: 10 Kasım, 09.05
blocks.text: One more date is marked in a very different way. Atatürk died in Dolmabahçe Palace in Istanbul at 9:05 in the morning on 10 November 1938. Every year at that minute, *dokuzu beş geçe*, sirens sound across the country, and people stop where they are, in classrooms, in the street and in their cars, for a minute of silence.
Mustafa Kemal took the surname Atatürk under the [Surname Law of 1934](a1-u03-culture). Here is a national day in the Turkish of this unit:

blocks.tr: Bugün 29 Ekim. Okullar kapalı. Sokaklarda çok bayrak var. Akşam saat dokuzda meydanda havai fişek var.
blocks.en: Today is 29 October. The schools are closed. There are a lot of flags in the streets. In the evening, at nine o'clock, there are fireworks in the square.

questions.q: Which date marks the proclamation of the Republic?
On 23 April, who takes the seats of mayors and ministers for a few hours?
questions.explain: 23 April is also Children's Day, *Çocuk Bayramı*.

questions.q: In the Turkish text, why does it say *çok bayrak* and not *çok bayraklar*?
options: After a quantity word the noun stays singular
questions.explain: *Çok* works like a number: *çok bayrak*, a lot of flags.

sources.title: 23 Nisan Ulusal Egemenlik ve Çocuk Bayramı
sources.note: Assembly opened in Ankara on 23 April 1920; holiday from 1921; Çocuk Bayramı from 1927; present name from Law 2429 of 1981; officials hand their seats to pupils; TRT's international children's festival

sources.title: Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day
sources.note: Landing at Samsun on 19 May 1919; Law 3466 of 20 June 1938; present name from 1981

sources.title: Victory Day (Turkey)
sources.note: Battle of Dumlupınar, 30 August 1922; first celebrated 1923; official holiday since 1926; Armed Forces Day

sources.title: Büyük Taarruz
sources.note: Offensive from 26 August 1922; Başkomutanlık Meydan Muharebesi on 30 August; İzmir reached on 9 September 1922

sources.title: Republic Day (Turkey)
sources.note: Proclamation on 29 October 1923; holiday from 1 pm on 28 October; morning parades, evening fireworks, the Bosphorus display

sources.title: Death and state funeral of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
sources.note: Died at 09:05 on 10 November 1938 in Dolmabahçe Palace

sources.title: Atatürk için 09.05'te hayat durdu
sources.note: Sirens and a minute of silence at 09.05 every 10 November; traffic stops
